title: Oil Prices Surge as Iran Strikes Targets Near Strait of Hormuz
excerpt: Crude benchmarks extend gains after Tehran confirms military operations against 'hostile targets' in the strategic waterway that handles a fifth of global oil shipments.
body:
• Iran confirmed military strikes against "hostile targets" near the Strait of Hormuz, sending oil prices sharply higher.
  • Multiple explosions were reported in southern Iran, with state media describing the operation as a response to threats in the strategic waterway.
  • The Strait of Hormuz handles roughly 20 percent of the world's oil shipments, making any military action there a trigger for global energy market volatility.
  • President Trump responded by saying the "war's got to end pretty soon," signaling U.S. concern over escalation.

Oil prices extended their gains on Thursday after Iran confirmed it had struck what it described as "hostile targets" in the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway through which roughly a fifth of the world's oil supply passes daily. The military action sent crude benchmarks sharply higher and reignited fears of a broader disruption to global energy flows.

Explosions Reported in Southern Iran

Multiple explosions were heard in southern Iran, with state-affiliated Fars News Agency reporting that Iranian forces had engaged hostile targets in the strait. The Anadolu Agency and Xinhua both confirmed reports of at least two explosions, describing the action as linked to an operation against unidentified hostile elements.

Details of the strikes remained sparse, with Iranian authorities providing limited information about the nature of the targets or the scale of the operation. No group or nation immediately claimed to be the target of the strikes, and regional governments had not issued formal responses in the hours following the reports.

Oil Markets React Swiftly

Crude oil benchmarks moved higher immediately after the reports emerged. The Strait of Hormuz is the world's most critical oil chokepoint, with approximately 17 to 21 million barrels per day transiting through its narrow passage between Iran and Oman. Any military activity in the area triggers immediate risk-premium adjustments across global energy markets.

"War's got to end pretty soon."

— President Donald Trump, responding to the Iran strikes

Bloomberg reported that oil extended earlier gains as traders priced in the heightened risk of supply disruption. Energy analysts noted that even a brief closure or partial blockage of the strait could remove millions of barrels from global supply, with cascading effects on gasoline prices, shipping costs, and inflation.

Strategic Implications for India and the Diaspora

The developments carry outsized significance for India, which imports more than 80 percent of its crude oil and relies heavily on supplies routed through the Strait of Hormuz. Any sustained disruption could push India's energy import bill sharply higher, with knock-on effects for inflation and the rupee.

For Indian Americans and the broader diaspora, the situation compounds existing concerns about fuel costs and economic stability. Higher oil prices typically translate into elevated gasoline prices at the pump in the United States and increased costs for goods transported by road and sea.

Escalation Risks

The strikes come amid heightened tensions in the broader Middle East, with the United States maintaining a significant naval presence in the Persian Gulf region. President Trump's remark that the conflict needs to end soon suggests Washington is monitoring the situation closely but has not signaled an imminent military response.

Shipping and insurance firms are expected to reassess risk ratings for vessels transiting the strait, which could drive up freight costs even if physical disruptions remain limited. The last major escalation in the strait, in 2019, saw tanker seizures and drone attacks that briefly spiked oil prices before diplomatic efforts de-escalated tensions.

Markets will be watching closely for any follow-up military action or diplomatic response in the coming hours.
